fact: Daz cast magic missiles and scorching rays during the assassination, using visual sighting and precise targeting; the spells struck the assassins with visible light and heat, but Zalthir’s Darkness concealed the flashes.
source_quote: Motes of light appear above his hand... a silent rush of air accompanies the flight of the magic missiles... the rush of intense heat as the fiery energy is manifested.

subject: Werz Saltbaron’s invisibility
fact: Werz Saltbaron becomes invisible after being healed by Grygum, confirming his identity as a covert operative.
source_quote: Zalthir watches as the Duergar becomes invisible.

subject: Zalthir

source_quote: Zalthir agrees and helps push the other body into the water.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir casts Darkness to cover the area and hides the flash of Daz’s scorching rays.
source_quote: Zalthir covers the area with Darkness.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir casts Darkness to cover the area and mutters that area-of-effect spells are useful because he can't see.
source_quote: Zalthir covers the area with Darkness. "I can't see. And this is why area of effect spells are useful," he mutters.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir finds a box of scented candles among the assassins' corpses and passes them to Thorin.
source_quote: Zalthir starts to rifle through the assassins' corpses and finds some coins, a pair of bloodstained gloves, and a box of candles. He notices they have a pleasant smell and passes them to Thorin.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir finds a charcoal drawing of the Duergar merchant on one of the assassins' corpses and presents it to him.
source_quote: Zalthir scrutinizes him and concludes that Holl may not have been lying... He presents it to the Duergar.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir finds coins, bloodstained gloves, and a box of scented candles among the assassins' corpses and passes the candles to Thorin.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir hears a body falling into the water and says, "We must get out of here before the guard shows up."
source_quote: Just then, Zalthir hears a body falling into the water. Grygum has pushed the first corpse into the water. "We must get out of here before the guard shows up."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir helps push the second assassin’s corpse into the water.
source_quote: Zalthir agrees and helps push the other body into the water.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir nods in agreement when Grygum says they have people looking for them.
source_quote: Zalthir nods, "Of course."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir offers to create an illusion of whale sounds for Thorin.
source_quote: Zalthir chuckles, "I could create that illusion for you."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir overhears Daz and asks Grygum if Themberchaud plays chess, recalling Milo Goodbarrel’s memoirs.
source_quote: Zalthir overhears Daz and asks Grygum, "Do you think this dragon also plays chess? According to Milo Goodbarrel’s memoirs, chess played a significant role in negotiating with the metallic dragons."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir reflects that deals with red dragons are never good deals.
source_quote: Deals with red dragons are never good deals," thinks Zalthir.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir says, "Convenient," after the Duergar merchant becomes invisible.
source_quote: Zalthir watches as the Duergar becomes invisible. "Convenient."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir says, "Deals with red dragons are never good deals," thinking to himself.
source_quote: Deals with red dragons are never good deals," thinks Zalthir.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir says, "I could create that illusion for you," offering to make whale sounds for Thorin.
source_quote: Zalthir chuckles, "I could create that illusion for you."

subject: Zalthir

source_quote: Just then, Zalthir hears a body falling into the water. Grygum has pushed the first corpse into the water. "We must get out of here before the guard shows up."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir watches the Duergar merchant become invisible after thanking them.
source_quote: Zalthir watches as the Duergar becomes invisible.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir wonders if Daz is lying about being from Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: Zalthir wonders as well. Daz says he is. But Zalthir isn’t convinced that is the truth.

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar are a reclusive subterranean race known for austere living conditions, dark clothing, and occasional displays of hidden wealth, and are suspected of internal conflict and possible involvement in psychic assassinations.
source_quote: The Ghohlbrorn’s Lair... offers the kind of accommodations one could expect from a Duergar: unpleasant, cold, and austere.

subject: Duergar City Watch
fact: The Duergar City Watch is referenced as the entity Thorin attempted to influence and direct during the incident with the stone giant, and whose official duties interference is seen as obstruction.
source_quote: Thorin attempted to influence and direct the actions of the Duergar City Watch during the aforementioned incident with the stone giant.

subject: Duergar City Watch
fact: The Duergar City Watch is the official law enforcement body of Gracklstugh, tasked with maintaining order and enforcing city ordinances. It is viewed as an authoritarian institution that tolerates no interference, and its authority is absolute. Thorin’s attempts to influence its actions are considered obstruction.

subject: Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts are a mysterious, possibly outlawed or hidden faction in Gracklstugh, whose existence is suspected but unconfirmed. Gartokkar demands proof of their involvement, indicating they are tied to a larger conspiracy, possibly involving the egg or Themberchaud.

subject: Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts are a secretive and dangerous faction responsible for stealing the red dragon egg and creating chaos in the Underdark. They are enemies of the Keepers of the Flame and are actively opposed by the Stone Guards.
source_quote: The Gray Ghosts stole the egg and created a great disturbance in the Underdark.

subject: Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts are referenced by Gartokkar as the group whose proof must be found alongside the egg.
source_quote: Gartokkar looks at him, 'Just find me the egg and the proof of the Gray Ghosts.'

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a Duergar psionic order that claims spiritual and political authority over Gracklstugh. They manipulate Themberchaud, orchestrate the theft of the red dragon egg, and use fabricated legal charges to control outsiders.
source_quote: The powers of the Keepers of the Flame derive an equal measure from our psionic abilities, the leadership of the Deepking, and our influence over Themberchaud.

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a powerful Duergar religious or political faction within Gracklstugh, associated with divine authority and the suppression of dissent. Thorin’s repeated questioning of their motives has marked him as a threat to their doctrinal control and social hierarchy.

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a secretive organization believed to be in possession of a Red Dragon held in peculiar captivity, and are the subject of Grygum and Daz’s intelligence-gathering efforts.
source_quote: Daz wants to learn about the Keepers of the Flame, and Grygum wants to know about this Red Dragon that is kept in some kind of peculiar captivity by the Keepers of the Flame.

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a secretive, ritualistic order based in the southeastern cave; they are subordinate to Themberchaud but act as the immediate authority over the agents, creating a dual-layered chain of command.
source_quote: Your first mission is to do whatever the Keepers of the Flame ask you to, but report to Themberchaud first.

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are referenced as the group Thorin has repeatedly questioned, and whose authority and motives are perceived as dissent and disrespect.
source_quote: Thorin has repeatedly questioned the authority and motives of various Duergar individuals and factions, including the Keepers of the Flame.

subject: Stone Guards
fact: The Stone Guards are an external force to which Grygum claims the group has ties; their existence introduces a third, potentially hostile layer of allegiance, making the group’s position ambiguous and precarious.
source_quote: We have people who will come looking for us!

subject: Stone Guards
fact: The Stone Guards are the official law enforcement of Gracklstugh, tasked with maintaining order and pursuing criminals like Droki. They are manipulated by the Keepers of the Flame and used as a threat against non-Duergar like Thorin.
source_quote: Well we will turn you over to the Stone Guards.

subject: The Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts are a rogue faction that stole the dragon egg intended to replace Themberchaud, destabilizing the balance of power in Gracklstugh, and are now hunted by both the Keepers of the Flame and the Stone Guards.
source_quote: The Gray Ghosts stole the egg and created a great disturbance in the Underdark.

subject: the Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts are a thieves’ guild that stole the red dragon egg intended to hatch Themberchaud’s replacement, causing a disturbance in the Underdark.
source_quote: We lost face when the Gray Ghosts stole the valuable red dragon egg that would hatch Themberchaud’s replacement.

subject: the Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a psionic faction that controls Themberchaud, believes he works for them, and seeks to replace him with a new dragon hatched from a stolen egg.
source_quote: Themberchaud thinks we work for him. What Themberchaud doesn’t realize is that he works for us.

subject: The Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a psionic sect in Gracklstugh that secretly control Themberchaud, manipulate agents through holy symbols and coercion, and are locked in a cold war with the Gray Ghosts over the stolen dragon egg meant to replace the current Wyrmsmith.
source_quote: We lost face when the Gray Ghosts stole the valuable red dragon egg that would hatch Themberchaud’s replacement.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a dragon, likely a red dragon, held in oppressive or exploitative conditions by the Duergar of Gracklstugh. Grygum’s outrage at its treatment and Thorin’s plan to ‘ride it out’ suggest it is not merely a beast but a sentient entity with symbolic or strategic value — possibly a prisoner, weapon, or sacred being.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is referenced by Grygum as the entity he is appalled at how they treat, and by Gartokkar as one of the city's affairs Thorin is suspected of gathering intelligence on.
source_quote: Grygum smiles, 'As a cleric of Bahamut, I am appalled at how they treat Themberchaud. Let’s do it.' ... Given his questioning and interest in the city's affairs, including the Keepers of the Flame and Themberchaud, Thorin is suspected of espionage...

subject: Themberchaud’s Agents
fact: Themberchaud believes he has recruited the party as his personal agents, but they are unaware they are being manipulated by the Keepers of the Flame, who use his authority as cover for their own agenda — making the party unwitting triple agents.
source_quote: Your first mission is to do whatever the Keepers of the Flame ask you to, but report to Themberchaud first.

subject: Themberchaud’s agents
fact: Themberchaud claims the group as his agents without consent, offering protection in exchange for obedience, but they are unaware he is himself manipulated.
source_quote: I am Themberchaud, and I wish for you to be my agent. And as my agents, you will have my protection.

subject: Themberchaud's Regime
fact: Themberchaud's regime operates as a coercive, personality-driven faction that assumes loyalty, offers protection as a privilege, and demands unquestioning obedience; its power is rooted in terror, illusion of choice, and the exploitation of agents' dependencies.
source_quote: You will have my protection.

subject: The Stone Guards
fact: The Stone Guards are Errde Blackskull’s enforcement arm, tasked with internal security, hunting the Gray Ghosts agent Droki, and suppressing knowledge of psychic assassins — a threat they believe is real but publicly deny.
source_quote: Errde, Captain of the Stone Guards, is looking for [Droki].

subject: the Stone Guards
fact: The Stone Guards are led by Errde Blackskull and are searching for Droki, an agent of the Gray Ghosts.
source_quote: This is the same person Errde, Captain of the Stone Guards, is looking for.

subject: Thieve’s Guild
fact: The Thieve’s Guild is in an ongoing war with the Keepers of the Flame, though the theft of the red dragon egg is attributed to the Gray Ghosts, suggesting possible misdirection or internal conflict.
source_quote: Our war with the Thieve’s guild has been ongoing.

subject: building that houses Gartokkar’s office
fact: The building that houses Gartokkar’s office is the location where Daz turns to Thorin while looking at his collection of badges, and where Thorin has a peculiar glint in his eye and turns to Grygum with his idea.
source_quote: As they stand outside the building that houses Gartokkar’s office, Daz turns to Thorin while looking at his collection of badges, 'So we flash the right one at the right time?' ... Thorin nods. And then he has a peculiar glint in his eye. He turns to Grygum, 'I have an idea. These factions are all trying to play us against each other, and this Dragon is one of us. So what if we ride this Dragon out of here, laying waste to everything behind us?'

subject: Cave of Gracklstugh
fact: The cave is a monumental, subterranean stronghold housing Themberchaud’s hoard, the Keepers of the Flame, and Gartokkar’s chambers; it is a nexus of power, deception, and layered loyalties.
source_quote: The Keepers of the Flame are in the far southeastern corner of the cave.

subject: Darklake
fact: The Darklake is a body of water near the piers where the assassination occurred, shrouded in darkness and used as a location for secretive encounters.
source_quote: A Duergar man appears, looking into the darkness of the Darklake.

subject: Gartokkar’s Chambers
fact: Gartokkar’s chambers are the site of ritualistic confirmation and political negotiation; it is where the group is formally acknowledged as agents, despite never having consented.
source_quote: I am so delighted to see that you accepted Themberchaud’s offer to be an agent of ours.

subject: Gartokkar’s chambers
fact: The Duergar priest sits down in his chamber and says, 'I am so delighted to see that you accepted Themberchaud’s offer to be an agent of ours.'
source_quote: The Duergar priest sits down in his chamber and says, 'I am so delighted to see that you accepted Themberchaud’s offer to be an agent of ours.'

subject: Gartokkar’s office
fact: Gartokkar’s office is the administrative center where Thorin’s case is managed. It is a place of negotiation, threat, and subtle control — the threshold between compliance and arrest. The events outside its doors mark the transition from passive interrogation to active rebellion.

subject: Gartokkar’s office
fact: Gartokkar’s office is the location referenced as the building they stand outside of, and where the conversation about the egg and the Gray Ghosts takes place.
source_quote: As they stand outside the building that houses Gartokkar’s office, Daz turns to Thorin while looking at his collection of badges... Gartokkar looks at him, 'Just find me the egg and the proof of the Gray Ghosts.'

subject: Ghohlbrorn’s Lair
fact: The Ghohlbrorn’s Lair offers the kind of accommodations one could expect from a Duergar: unpleasant, cold, and austere.
source_quote: The Ghohlbrorn’s Lair, to Daz’s refined sensibilities, offers the kind of accommodations one could expect from a Duergar: unpleasant, cold, and austere.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is a Duergar city ruled by hidden power structures: the Keepers of the Flame control Themberchaud, the Stone Guards enforce silence, and invisible assassins operate in the shadows — all while the populace remains unaware of the true rulers.
source_quote: Having invisible ruthless guards helps.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is a Duergar-dominated city in the Underdark governed by strict hierarchy, suspicion of outsiders, and secret power struggles. Law enforcement is arbitrary, and authority is maintained through fear, manipulation, and fabricated charges.
source_quote: With them, you can travel within Gracklstugh, but there are limits.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is a rigid, hierarchical Duergar city where non-Duergar are under constant suspicion, authority is absolute, and dissent is crushed. Its laws are enforced with discretion, and survival depends on navigating its bureaucracy, avoiding association with undesirables, and concealing forbidden knowledge — especially regarding the egg and Themberchaud.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is referenced as the hierarchical society where questioning authority is not tolerated, and where unauthorized access and association with undesirables are violations of city ordinances.
source_quote: Such questioning can be perceived as dissent and disrespect, which is not tolerated within Gracklstugh's hierarchical society. ... Any unauthorized access to restricted areas is a violation of city ordinances. ... Such associations can raise suspicion and lead to accusations of conspiracy, aiding, and abetting.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: With them, you can travel within Gracklstugh, but there are limits.
source_quote: With them, you can travel within Gracklstugh, but there are limits.

subject: Shattered Spire
fact: Come by the Shattered Spire tomorrow, and I will reward you.
source_quote: Come by the Shattered Spire tomorrow, and I will reward you.

subject: Shattered Spire
fact: The Shattered Spire is a location referenced by Werz Saltbaron as a place to receive a reward, suggesting it is a known hub for clandestine dealings among Duergar elites.
source_quote: Come by the Shattered Spire tomorrow, and I will reward you.

subject: the Ghohlbrorn’s Lair
fact: The Ghohlbrorn’s Lair contains a large, cold, damp dining room and communal chambers where you can sleep.
source_quote: There is a large, cold, damp dining room and communal chambers where you can sleep

subject: The Ghohlbrorn’s Lair
fact: The Ghohlbrorn’s Lair is a cold, austere Duergar stronghold with a large damp dining room and communal sleeping chambers, serving as a temporary refuge for escapees.
source_quote: The Ghohlbrorn’s Lair... offers the kind of accommodations one could expect from a Duergar: unpleasant, cold, and austere.

subject: The Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are in the far southeastern corner of the cave, and the journey is uneventful.
source_quote: The Keepers of the Flame are in the far southeastern corner of the cave, and the journey is uneventful.

subject: the Keepers of the Flame’s chamber
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are located in the far southeastern corner of the cave, accessible via Errde Blackskull’s passes.
source_quote: The Keepers of the Flame are in the far southeastern corner of the cave, and the journey is uneventful.

subject: The Keepers of the Flame’s Chamber
fact: The Keepers of the Flame operate from a stone-carved chamber near the monumental cave entrance, where they manipulate the party using holy symbols, psionic authority, and the illusion of divine mandate.
source_quote: Gartokkar hands out some gold badges.

subject: Themberchaud’s Hoard Cavern
fact: Themberchaud’s cavern is a glittering prison of gold and gems, where the dragon is pampered, sedentary, and utterly unaware he is a captive — a symbol of the Keepers’ control over even the most powerful beings.
source_quote: Sitting on top of it is a plump, overweight red dragon.

subject: Themberchaud’s hoard-cavern
fact: Themberchaud’s cavern is filled with a hoard of gems and coins, and he sits atop it, visibly overweight and pampered.
source_quote: The dragon’s cavern is filled with a hoard of gems and coins. Sitting on top of it is a plump, overweight red dragon.

subject: the piers near the 'inn'
fact: On one of the piers, a Duergar man appears, looking into the darkness of the Darklake, wearing dark and plain clothes with occasional flourishes of wealth and taste.
source_quote: On one of the piers, a Duergar man appears, looking into the darkness of the Darklake. Like most Duergar, his clothes are dark and plain, but there is the occasional flourish of wealth and taste

subject: the Shattered Spire
fact: The Shattered Spire is the location Werz Saltbaron invites the group to for a reward.
source_quote: Come by the Shattered Spire tomorrow, and I will reward you.

subject: The Shattered Spire
fact: The Shattered Spire is the rumored meeting place of Werz Saltbaron, possibly a front for Gray Ghost operations or a safehouse for agents — now a potential destination for the party after his cryptic invitation.
source_quote: Come by the Shattered Spire tomorrow, and I will reward you.

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is the vast subterranean realm where Themberchaud resides and where the red dragon egg was stolen. It is a place of ancient power, hidden factions, and shifting loyalties.
source_quote: The Gray Ghosts stole the egg and created a great disturbance in the Underdark.

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: Dragon
fact: The Dragon is referenced by Thorin as the entity that is one of us, and that they may ride out of the city, laying waste to everything behind them.
source_quote: Thorin turns to Grygum, 'I have an idea. These factions are all trying to play us against each other, and this Dragon is one of us. So what if we ride this Dragon out of here, laying waste to everything behind us?'

subject: Droki
fact: We have identified an agent of the Grey Ghosts. His name is Droki.
source_quote: We have identified an agent of the Grey Ghosts. His name is Droki.

subject: Kenku Whistler
fact: The Kenku Whistler is referenced in Milo Goodbarrel’s book as having used psychic blades to fake an attack, suggesting the technique is known and possibly replicable.
source_quote: Milo describes this kind of attack as a psychic blade attack... where the Kenku Whistler used the psychic blades to fake an attack by Milo on an enemy.

subject: Psychic Assassins
fact: Psychic assassins are unseen killers who strike without physical wounds, leaving victims dead with no entrance or exit trauma, their method confirmed by Zalthir’s observation and Daz’s novel-based recognition — possibly linked to the Gray Ghosts.
source_quote: The bodies were found with no exit wounds or entrance wounds.

subject: Psychic Assassins
fact: Two psychic assassins attacked Werz Saltbaron using glowing, non-physical weapons that leave no entrance or exit wounds, and vanished without leaving any weapons behind.
source_quote: Two assassins, wearing face coverings and wielding glowing weapons, strike the other man.

subject: psychic blade attack
fact: Milo describes this kind of attack as a psychic blade attack. It leaves no trace. There is this one moment where the Kenku Whistler used the psychic blades to fake an attack by Milo on an enemy.
source_quote: Milo describes this kind of attack as a psychic blade attack. It leaves no trace. There is this one moment where the Kenku Whistler used the psychic blades to fake an attack by Milo on an enemy.

subject: stone giant
fact: A deranged stone giant was involved in a public altercation with Thorin, triggering the initial charges against him. Its presence suggests either a breach in city security, a magical anomaly, or a weaponized entity — possibly connected to the Gray Ghosts or the egg.

subject: stone giant
fact: The stone giant is referenced as the deranged entity Thorin was involved in the altercation with, and whose actions contributed to the ensuing public disorder.
source_quote: Thorin was involved in the altercation with the deranged stone giant.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: The dragon’s cavern is filled with a hoard of gems and coins. Sitting on top of it is a plump, overweight red dragon.
source_quote: The dragon’s cavern is filled with a hoard of gems and coins. Sitting on top of it is a plump, overweight red dragon.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a bloated, out-of-shape red dragon kept in a hoard-filled cavern, unable to hunt or survive in the wild, and unaware he is a captive pawn being prepared for replacement by the Keepers of the Flame.
source_quote: His massive body gives the distinct impression that he is overweight, indicating eating habits that don’t bode well.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a dragon of immense power and ancient will, currently unaware that he is being manipulated. He is not a puppet but a being who chooses to move on — a choice the Keepers exploit to maintain control.
source_quote: Eventually, the Dragon moves on because he wants to see more of the world.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a massive, overweight red dragon, the Wyrmsmith of Gracklstugh, whose physical condition suggests extreme pampering and loss of survival instincts; he is a terrifying, manipulative predator who uses psychological dominance to control agents.
source_quote: I never liked gold dragons. If I catch anyone spying, I will kill them.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz claims to be from Menzoberranzan, but Zalthir doubts his truthfulness; he has experience with drow politics and understands that factional loyalty is performative, not absolute.
source_quote: The faction thinks we are working for them. Whether we do is up to us.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a Duergar agent who carries a collection of official badges and instructs Thorin on their tactical use, suggesting he is involved in surveillance, access control, or covert operations within Gracklstugh. His demeanor indicates familiarity with bureaucratic manipulation and enforcement protocols.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a book-obsessed human who reads voraciously and recognizes the psychic blade attacks from Milo Goodbarrel’s novel, and actively seeks intelligence on the Keepers of the Flame and the Red Dragon’s captivity.
source_quote: Milo describes this kind of attack as a psychic blade attack. It leaves no trace. There is this one moment where the Kenku Whistler used the psychic blades to fake an attack by Milo on an enemy.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a member of Thorin’s group who understands the political symbolism of faction badges and recognizes the need to use them strategically to navigate Gracklstugh’s dangerous bureaucracy.
source_quote: So we flash the right one at the right time?

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a novel enthusiast who reads Milo Goodbarrel’s book and recognizes the psychic blade attack as described in fiction, and claims to be from Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: Milo describes this kind of attack as a psychic blade attack. It leaves no trace. There is this one moment where the Kenku Whistler used the psychic blades to fake an attack by Milo on an enemy.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a voracious reader of fantasy literature, believes in the existence of psychic blades from novels, and is the group’s strategist who manipulates perception to navigate factional politics, claiming ties to Menzoberranzan to gain the dragon’s trust.
source_quote: Milo describes this kind of attack as a psychic blade attack. It leaves no trace.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is known for his fondness of novels and has read Milo Goodbarrel’s book detailing the events surrounding the war of the dragon.
source_quote: Daz, known for his fondness of novels, reads voraciously and has managed to get a copy of Milo Goodbarrel’s book detailing the events surrounding the war of the dragon.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is referenced by Thorin as the one who turns to him while looking at his collection of badges and says, 'So we flash the right one at the right time?'
source_quote: Daz turns to Thorin while looking at his collection of badges, 'So we flash the right one at the right time?'

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is an agent of the Gray Ghosts and the target of both the Stone Guards and the Keepers of the Flame.
source_quote: We have identified an agent of the Grey Ghosts. His name is Droki.

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is an agent of the Gray Ghosts, identified by Gartokkar as the thief of the red dragon egg. He is the same individual sought by Errde, Captain of the Stone Guards, linking multiple factions to the theft.
source_quote: We have identified an agent of the Grey Ghosts. His name is Droki.

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is an agent of the Gray Ghosts, identified by the Keepers of the Flame as the same person Errde Blackskull is seeking.
source_quote: We have identified an agent of the Grey Ghosts. His name is Droki.

subject: Errde
fact: Errde is the Captain of the Stone Guards and is actively pursuing Droki, the Gray Ghosts agent who stole the red dragon egg. His investigation intersects with Gartokkar’s covert operations.
source_quote: Thorin remembers that this is the same person Errde, Captain of the Stone Guards, is looking for.

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull is a paranoid Duergar who denies the existence of psychic assassins but hints at government cover-ups, and has lost two clan members to unexplained deaths with no entrance or exit wounds.
source_quote: Oh, just an old wives tale to frighten children. They kill people with their minds. Of course, this is nonsense. They are just another figment of the people’s imagination. It’s more likely that they don’t exist, and instead, assassinations are being conducted by some agency in the government, and this is a cover.

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull is referenced by Grygum as the authority who decides the fate of failed Drow, and she is the captain of the Stone Guards.
source_quote: Errde Blackskull might decide his fate should be precisely like Serith's

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull is the Captain of the Stone Guards, paranoid about psychic assassins, and publicly dismisses them as folklore while privately directing investigations into the deaths of her clan members.
source_quote: I would appreciate it if you were to look for the empty scabbard killers. My underlings have reported their presence after finding bodies with puzzling wounds.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar is a Duergar official who oversees Thorin’s case and enforces city ordinances with discretionary severity. He warns Thorin that revealing the existence of the egg would be a disaster, implying he is aware of its significance and seeks its recovery, possibly to leverage it for political or personal gain.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar is a Duergar priest who serves Themberchaud with reverence despite his evident displeasure; he acts as the dragon’s intermediary and enforces the dragon’s will through ritual and badge distribution.
source_quote: Foreigners, meet the Father of Flame, the Everburning, and the Foundry’s Heart — Themberchaud, the Wyrmsmith of Gracklstugh.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar is a Duergar priest who serves the Keepers of the Flame and reveals that Themberchaud believes he is in control, but the Keepers are manipulating him.
source_quote: Themberchaud thinks we work for him. What Themberchaud doesn’t realize is that he works for us.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar is referenced by Thorin as the one who looks at him and says, 'Just find me the egg and the proof of the Gray Ghosts.'
source_quote: Gartokkar looks at him, 'Just find me the egg and the proof of the Gray Ghosts.'

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar is referenced by Thorin as the one who turns dark and then smiles, saying that sharing the egg would be a disaster.
source_quote: Gartokkar turns dark and then smiles, 'You joke? Sharing that would be a disaster.'

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar is the Duergar priest and Custodian of the Flame who manipulates the party into servitude under the guise of holy duty, secretly controls Themberchaud, and hides the theft of the dragon egg meant to replace him.
source_quote: Themberchaud thinks we work for him. What Themberchaud doesn’t realize is that he works for us.

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn is the Custodian of the Flame and leader of the Keepers of the Flame, secretly manipulating Themberchaud while pretending to serve him. He holds authority over Gracklstugh’s internal security and is willing to fabricate charges against non-Duergar to maintain control.
source_quote: Themberchaud thinks we work for him. What Themberchaud doesn’t realize is that he works for us.

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn is the Custodian of the Flame who manipulates the group by threatening them with the Stone Guards if they refuse to serve the Keepers.
source_quote: Well we will turn you over to the Stone Guards.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum has pushed corpses into water and is aware of the group’s entanglement in multiple conflicting loyalties; he suspects they are double or triple agents and voices confusion about their true allegiance.
source_quote: I suppose we are double agents, or is it triple agents? We work for the Stone Guards and the Keepers of the Flame.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric of Bahamut who is appalled by the treatment of Themberchaud and has aligned himself with Thorin’s radical plan to use the dragon as a weapon against Gracklstugh’s hierarchy. His faith positions him as a moral counterpoint to Duergar orthodoxy, and his willingness to destroy the city suggests deep disillusionment.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric of Bahamut who is horrified by the exploitation of Themberchaud and has aligned with Thorin’s plan to free the dragon and dismantle the Duergar hierarchy.
source_quote: As a cleric of Bahamut, I am appalled at how they treat Themberchaud. Let’s do it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a determined investigator who discovered scrolls tied to Errde’s goods, actively probes the mystery of the woundless deaths, and now serves as a double agent under Themberchaud while ostensibly working for the Keepers of the Flame.
source_quote: I liked the books. They were well written.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a persistent investigator who found scrolls among Errde’s goods and is obsessed with uncovering the truth behind the psychic blade attacks and the Red Dragon’s captivity by the Keepers of the Flame.
source_quote: I liked the books. They were well written.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a warrior who investigates the assassins, uses magic missiles and healing spells, and is determined to uncover the truth behind the deaths.
source_quote: Grygum rushes one of the assassins, trying to toss him into the water. He fails.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is appalled at how Themberchaud is treated and is willing to act against the city’s authorities.
source_quote: Grygum smiles, 'As a cleric of Bahamut, I am appalled at how they treat Themberchaud. Let’s do it.'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is perplexed by the dead bodies with no entrance or exit wounds and no evidence of foul play.
source_quote: Grygum is perplexed: dead bodies with no entrance or exit wounds, no evidence of foul play, just dead bodies.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced as a cleric of Bahamut who is appalled at how Themberchaud is treated, and who agrees to ride the Dragon out of the city.
source_quote: Grygum smiles, 'As a cleric of Bahamut, I am appalled at how they treat Themberchaud. Let’s do it.'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by Thorin as the one who smiles and says, 'As a cleric of Bahamut, I am appalled at how they treat Themberchaud. Let’s do it.'
source_quote: Grygum smiles, 'As a cleric of Bahamut, I am appalled at how they treat Themberchaud. Let’s do it.'

subject: Holl Forgebrand
fact: Holl Forgebrand is a blunt Duergar subordinate of Errde who confirmed the bodies had no entrance or exit wounds, and supports the theory that the killings are the work of unseen psychic assassins.
source_quote: The bodies were found with no exit wounds or entrance wounds.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar asks when they will be able to leave and shrugs when Daz says they should stay.
source_quote: Jimjar has made a few friends and asks - "When do you expect us to be able to leave?"... Jimjar shrugs and slumps into one of the beds. He sighs, "Very well."

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a massive, overweight red dragon kept in captivity by the Keepers of the Flame, unaware he is being groomed for replacement, and believes himself to be the sovereign master of his agents — a delusion the priests exploit.
source_quote: I wish to speak to them alone.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a massive, overweight red dragon who rules as the Wyrmsmith of Gracklstugh; he assumes loyalty, demands obedience, and uses psychological manipulation to bind agents through fear and perceived privilege.
source_quote: I wish to speak to them alone. If I catch anyone spying, I will kill them.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a powerful dragon believed by the Duergar to be a sovereign ruler of the Underdark, but in reality he is a pawn being guided by Gartokkar and the Keepers of the Flame. He is unaware of the manipulation and believes he is in command.
source_quote: Eventually, the Dragon moves on because he wants to see more of the world.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is an overweight red dragon, the 'Father of Flame' and 'Wyrmsmith of Gracklstugh', kept in captivity and unaware he is being manipulated by the Keepers of the Flame.
source_quote: I am Themberchaud, and I wish for you to be my agent. And as my agents, you will have my protection.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin has picked up the peculiar antipathy towards dragons that giants have, and Themberchaud is triggering him.
source_quote: Having lived with giants, Thorin has picked up the peculiar antipathy towards dragons that giants have. And this red dragon is triggering him.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf with a deep antipathy toward dragons, who questions the legitimacy of their forced recruitment and insists on being his own faction.
source_quote: I want to be my faction.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a giant-scarred warrior who resents dragons, refuses to accept passive subjugation, and demands clarity on the terms of his coerced allegiance to Themberchaud and the Keepers of the Flame, ultimately recognizing the group is trapped in a triple-agent web.
source_quote: I want to be my faction.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a non-Duergar surface dweller involved in public disturbances, interference with the Duergar City Watch, and repeated questioning of Duergar authority, including the Keepers of the Flame. He is suspected of unauthorized access, association with undesirables, espionage, and possession of contraband. His actions have drawn the suspicion of Gracklstugh's authorities, who may imprison him for any perceived threat to stability.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a surface dwarf who has been recruited into the political machinations of Gracklstugh. He is under suspicion by multiple factions, has been offered holy relics to gain access to restricted areas, and is now being threatened with fabricated charges under Duergar law.
source_quote: I am just putting all of our cards on the table. So if we get arrested, we will have to tell the Stone Guards about the egg, right?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is exasperated by the layered factions and wants to be his own faction.
source_quote: Thorin is exasperated and almost shouts, "I am sorry, I can't deal with these factions. I can't keep track of who we are working for and which faction we are double-crossing. I want to be my faction."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced by Gartokkar as the one who puts all of our cards on the table, so if we get arrested, we will have to tell the Stone Guards about the egg.
source_quote: Thorin stares at him. 'I am just putting all of our cards on the table. So if we get arrested, we will have to tell the Stone Guards about the egg, right?'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced by Grygum as the one who has a peculiar glint in his eye, turns to him, and says, 'I have an idea. These factions are all trying to play us against each other, and this Dragon is one of us. So what if we ride this Dragon out of here, laying waste to everything behind us?'
source_quote: Thorin nods. And then he has a peculiar glint in his eye. He turns to Grygum, 'I have an idea. These factions are all trying to play us against each other, and this Dragon is one of us. So what if we ride this Dragon out of here, laying waste to everything behind us?'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wants to ride the Dragon out of Gracklstugh, laying waste to everything behind him.
source_quote: Thorin nods. And then he has a peculiar glint in his eye. He turns to Grygum, 'I have an idea. These factions are all trying to play us against each other, and this Dragon is one of us. So what if we ride this Dragon out of here, laying waste to everything behind us?'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin, having lived with giants, harbors a deep antipathy toward dragons and is exasperated by the layered factional manipulation; he resists being forced into allegiance and seeks to become his own faction.
source_quote: I want to be my faction.

subject: Werz Saltbaron
fact: Werz Saltbaron is a Duergar merchant who becomes invisible after being rescued, and a charcoal drawing of him is found on one of the assassins' corpses.
source_quote: Oh my, I was. I am Werz Saltbaron. And you did me a good turn. Come by the Shattered Spire tomorrow, and I will reward you. Today, I have places to be.

subject: Werz Saltbaron
fact: Werz Saltbaron is a Duergar merchant who faked an assassination attempt to gain the party’s trust, later vanishes via invisibility, and was likely the target — or the assassin — in a plot tied to the Gray Ghosts and the stolen dragon egg.
source_quote: Oh my, I was.

subject: Werz Saltbaron
fact: Werz Saltbaron is a Duergar merchant who was attacked by invisible assassins wielding psychic weapons, has no physical wounds, and later vanishes invisibly after being healed by Grygum.
source_quote: Oh my, I was. I am Werz Saltbaron. And you did me a good turn. Come by the Shattered Spire tomorrow, and I will reward you. Today, I have places to be.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a bronze dragonborn who observes the manipulation of Themberchaud, finds the assassins' belongings, and considers creating illusions for Thorin.
source_quote: I could create that illusion for you.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a cautious spellcaster who casts Darkness and scorching rays during the assassination attempt, and later questions the morality of their actions after finding a charcoal drawing of the victim on an assassin’s body.
source_quote: I can’t see. And this is why area of effect spells are useful.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a gold dragonborn who was recruited as an agent by Themberchaud after being presented with no real choice, and now questions the dragon's sustainability, origins, and the feasibility of his regime.
source_quote: You are a gold dragonborn? No, a bronze. Good. I never liked gold dragons.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a pragmatic spellcaster who observes patterns in violence, confirms the existence of woundless deaths, casts area-control magic in combat, and uncovers the deception of the Duergar merchant Werz Saltbaron, who is likely an assassin.
source_quote: Convenient.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is uncertain if they made the right decision in intervening in the assassination.
source_quote: Zalthir stares at the merchant and the dead assassins. Zalthir is uncertain if they made the right decision.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir reflects that having invisible ruthless guards helps make the city peaceful and wonders if such a regime could be implemented.
source_quote: Zalthir reflects on the city's quiet and how the monks would be astounded at how peaceful it could be. "Having invisible ruthless guards helps." He wonders if such a regime could be implemented.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thinks, "Convenient," after seeing the Duergar merchant become invisible.
source_quote: Zalthir watches as the Duergar becomes invisible. "Convenient."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir wonders whether the overweight red dragon Themberchaud could survive in the wild, having forgotten how to hunt.
source_quote: Zalthir is stunned. He’s never seen such a thing... And then, he wonders whether this red dragon could survive in the wild. It is so pampered that it probably has forgotten how to hunt.

subject: bloodstained gloves
fact: A pair of bloodstained gloves is found among the assassins' corpses.
source_quote: Zalthir starts to rifle through the assassins' corpses and finds some coins, a pair of bloodstained gloves, and a box of candles.

subject: Bloodstained Gloves
fact: Bloodstained gloves recovered from the assassins suggest direct physical contact during killings — contradicting the theory of purely psychic attacks and hinting at hybrid methods or staged evidence.
source_quote: finds some coins, a pair of bloodstained gloves, and a box of candles.

subject: bloodstained gloves
fact: He finds some coins, a pair of bloodstained gloves, and a box of candles.
source_quote: He finds some coins, a pair of bloodstained gloves, and a box of candles.

subject: box of candles
fact: A box of candles is found among the assassins' belongings; they have a pleasant smell and are passed to Thorin.
source_quote: He notices they have a pleasant smell and passes them to Thorin.

subject: Charcoal Drawing
fact: A charcoal drawing of Werz Saltbaron was found on the body of one of the assassins, confirming he was the targeted victim and linking him to the attack.
source_quote: He presents it to the Duergar. 'Oh my, I was.'

subject: charcoal drawing
fact: He does find a charcoal drawing of the merchant on one of the bodies.
source_quote: He does find a charcoal drawing of the merchant on one of the bodies.

subject: Charcoal Drawing of Werz Saltbaron
fact: A charcoal drawing of Werz Saltbaron found on an assassin’s corpse suggests he was either the target of the attack — or the one who commissioned it — deepening the mystery of his true identity.
source_quote: He presents it to the Duergar. 'Oh my, I was.'

subject: charcoal drawing of Werz Saltbaron
fact: A charcoal drawing of Werz Saltbaron is found on one of the assassins' corpses, confirming he was the target.
source_quote: He presents it to the Duergar. 'Oh my, I was.'

subject: collection of badges
fact: The collection of badges carried by Daz represents official permissions, access levels, and authority tiers within Gracklstugh’s bureaucratic system. They are tools of control, used to navigate restricted zones and manipulate enforcement. Their selective use is critical to survival within the city’s layered hierarchy.

subject: collection of badges
fact: The collection of badges is referenced by Daz as the item he is looking at when asking Thorin if they should flash the right one at the right time.
source_quote: Daz turns to Thorin while looking at his collection of badges, 'So we flash the right one at the right time?'

subject: egg
fact: The egg is referenced by Gartokkar as the item that must be found, along with the proof of the Gray Ghosts, to avoid disaster.
source_quote: Gartokkar looks at him, 'Just find me the egg and the proof of the Gray Ghosts.'

subject: gold badges
fact: Gartokkar hands out some gold badges. Thorin weighs it in his hands.
source_quote: Gartokkar hands out some gold badges. Thorin weighs it in his hands.

subject: Gold Badges
fact: The gold badges are physical tokens of Themberchaud’s authority, distributed by Gartokkar to signify enrollment as an agent; their exact weight and value are unknown, but they carry immense symbolic weight.
source_quote: How much gold is this?

subject: gold badges of Themberchaud
fact: Gold badges bearing Themberchaud’s profile are handed out by Gartokkar to the group as symbols of their new status as agents.
source_quote: Give these humanoids some of the gold badges… and the rest of you do what Gartokkar says.

subject: Gold Badges of Themberchaud
fact: The gold badges bearing Themberchaud’s profile are both a symbol of authority and a tool of control — granting limited access to Gracklstugh while binding the wearer to the dragon’s claimed patronage.
source_quote: Give these humanoids some of the gold badges.

subject: gold pins with Themberchaud’s profile
fact: These gold pins, depicting Themberchaud’s likeness, were given to Thorin alongside the holy symbol. They serve as both a sign of favor and a means of surveillance, tying Thorin to the mythos of the dragon.
source_quote: let me give you this holy symbol of Laduguer and these gold pins featuring Themberchaud’s profile.

subject: holy symbol of Laduguer
fact: A holy symbol of Laduguer is given to the group by Gartokkar to aid in travel within Gracklstugh.
source_quote: Let me give you this holy symbol of Laduguer and these gold pins featuring Themberchaud’s profile.

subject: holy symbol of Laduguer
fact: A holy symbol of Laduguer was offered to Thorin by Gartokkar as a token granting limited access to Gracklstugh. It is likely a tool of control, meant to bind Thorin to the Keepers' authority.
source_quote: let me give you this holy symbol of Laduguer and these gold pins featuring Themberchaud’s profile.

subject: holy symbol of Laduguer
fact: Let me give you this holy symbol of Laduguer and these gold pins featuring Themberchaud’s profile.
source_quote: Let me give you this holy symbol of Laduguer and these gold pins featuring Themberchaud’s profile.

subject: Holy Symbol of Laduguer
fact: The holy symbol of Laduguer, the Duergar god of endurance and survival, is given to the party as a token of the Keepers’ divine mandate — yet its presence in the hands of manipulators suggests religious authority is being weaponized.
source_quote: Let me give you this holy symbol of Laduguer...

subject: magic missiles
fact: When Daz utters the mystical words, motes of light appear above his hand, and three fingers point at one of the assassins. A silent rush of air accompanies the flight of the magic missiles, and when they strike, a burst of light and a crackling sound fills the area.
source_quote: When Daz utters the mystical words, motes of light appear above his hand, and three fingers point at one of the assassins. A silent rush of air accompanies the flight of the magic missiles, and when they strike, a burst of light and a crackling sound fills the area.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel’s book
fact: Milo Goodbarrel’s book details the war of the dragon and describes psychic blade attacks, including the Kenku Whistler using them to fake an attack.
source_quote: Milo describes this kind of attack as a psychic blade attack. It leaves no trace. There is this one moment where the Kenku Whistler used the psychic blades to fake an attack by Milo on an enemy.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel’s memoirs
fact: According to Milo Goodbarrel’s memoirs, chess played a significant role in negotiating with the metallic dragons.
source_quote: According to Milo Goodbarrel’s memoirs, chess played a significant role in negotiating with the metallic dragons.

subject: passes
fact: The passes are referenced as the items Thorin may have used to enter restricted areas, though such access is still unauthorized and a violation.
source_quote: Depending on his movements within the city, Thorin may have entered areas restricted to non-Duergar citizens without proper authorization, even with the passes.

subject: proof of the Gray Ghosts
fact: The proof of the Gray Ghosts is referenced by Gartokkar as the item that must be found, along with the egg, to avoid disaster.
source_quote: Gartokkar looks at him, 'Just find me the egg and the proof of the Gray Ghosts.'

subject: Psychic Blades
fact: Psychic blades are non-physical weapons that kill without leaving entrance or exit wounds, and are described in novels as leaving only a moment of silent, invisible energy.
source_quote: Milo describes this kind of attack as a psychic blade attack. It leaves no trace.

subject: scented candles
fact: He notices they have a pleasant smell and passes them to Thorin. The dwarf smiles, 'Scented candles!'
source_quote: He notices they have a pleasant smell and passes them to Thorin. The dwarf smiles, 'Scented candles!'

subject: Scented Candles
fact: Scented candles found on the assassins’ bodies emit a pleasant aroma — possibly used to mask other odors, induce trance states, or signal covert meetings — a subtle clue to the assassins’ methods and affiliations.
source_quote: He notices they have a pleasant smell and passes them to Thorin.

subject: scorching rays
fact: He speaks the words for scorching rays and feels the rush of intense heat as the fiery energy is manifested. He points with his index finger, uses his thumb to sight, squints, and lets the rays loose. They travel quickly, leaving a streak of heat haze.
source_quote: He speaks the words for scorching rays and feels the rush of intense heat as the fiery energy is manifested. He points with his index finger, uses his thumb to sight, squints, and lets the rays loose. They travel quickly, leaving a streak of heat haze.

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: the egg
fact: The egg is a mysterious, highly sensitive artifact sought by Gartokkar and possibly tied to Themberchaud, the Gray Ghosts, or an ancient power. Its revelation is considered catastrophic, implying it holds the key to destabilizing Gracklstugh’s regime, awakening a dormant force, or exposing a forbidden truth.

subject: Themberchaud’s Hoard
fact: The hoard is a vast pile of gems and coins upon which Themberchaud rests; it symbolizes his wealth, power, and the decadence of his rule, contrasting sharply with the wild, self-sufficient dragons of legend.
source_quote: The dragon’s cavern is filled with a hoard of gems and coins.

subject: Chess and Dragon Diplomacy
fact: Zalthir wonders whether Themberchaud plays chess, referencing Milo Goodbarrel’s memoirs; this thread suggests the group is trying to interpret the dragon’s behavior through the lens of outdated metallic dragon protocols, possibly misreading his motives.
source_quote: Do you think this dragon also plays chess? According to Milo Goodbarrel’s memoirs, chess played a significant role in negotiating with the metallic dragons.

subject: Daz’s Origin
fact: Daz claims to be from Menzoberranzan, but Zalthir doubts his truth; the ambiguity of his background introduces uncertainty about his loyalty, potential blackmail vulnerabilities, and whether he is a spy or a double agent.
source_quote: Daz says he is. But Zalthir isn’t convinced that is the truth.

subject: Disappearance of Topsy and Turvy
fact: Topsy and Turvy have vanished without trace, leading Daz to suspect wererats, but no evidence or confirmation of their fate has been found.
source_quote: The other escapees, except for Topsy and Turvy, have gone missing. 'Wererats,' thinks Daz.

subject: Droki's identity
fact: Gartokkar identifies Droki as an agent of the Grey Ghosts, the same person Errde Blackskull is looking for, but his true allegiance remains unconfirmed.
source_quote: We have identified an agent of the Grey Ghosts. His name is Droki.

subject: Factional Identity Crisis
fact: The group is trapped in a web of overlapping, conflicting loyalties — Themberchaud, the Keepers of the Flame, the Stone Guards — and struggles to define whether they are agents, double agents, or none at all; Thorin’s desire to be 'his own faction' reflects a deeper existential rebellion.
source_quote: I can’t keep track of who we are working for and which faction we are double-crossing. I want to be my faction.

subject: Origin of Psychic Blades
fact: The origin and source of the psychic blade attacks remain unknown, with conflicting theories ranging from ancient Kenku techniques to government operatives, and no physical evidence has been recovered.
source_quote: They kill people with their minds... It’s more likely that they don’t exist... assassinations are being conducted by some agency in the government...

subject: proof of the Gray Ghosts
fact: The existence and activities of the Gray Ghosts remain unverified, but Gartokkar insists on proof. Their connection to the egg, Themberchaud, or the city’s hidden power structures is a central unresolved mystery that could expose a conspiracy or trigger civil unrest.

subject: Red Dragon’s Captivity
fact: The Red Dragon’s captivity by the Keepers of the Flame is unverified, but is the central focus of Grygum’s investigation, with no known witnesses or documentation yet uncovered.
source_quote: Grygum wants to know about this Red Dragon that is kept in some kind of peculiar captivity by the Keepers of the Flame.

subject: the egg
fact: The egg is a key object that Gartokkar demands, but its location and nature are not specified in this session.
source_quote: Gartokkar looks at him, 'Just find me the egg and the proof of the Gray Ghosts.'

subject: The Identity of Droki
fact: Droki, the Gray Ghosts agent sought by both Errde and Gartokkar, remains unidentified — but the party now possesses the knowledge that he is a key to the stolen egg and the psychic assassinations.
source_quote: We have identified an agent of the Grey Ghosts. His name is Droki.

subject: Themberchaud's replacement
fact: The Keepers of the Flame stole the red dragon egg that would hatch Themberchaud’s replacement, but Themberchaud is unaware of its existence.
source_quote: We lost face when the Gray Ghosts stole the valuable red dragon egg that would hatch Themberchaud’s replacement.

subject: Themberchaud’s Replacement
fact: The stolen dragon egg is the key to Themberchaud’s eventual replacement — but who will hatch from it? Will it be loyal to the Keepers? Or will it break free? And what happens if Themberchaud learns the truth?
source_quote: Eventually, the Dragon moves on because he wants to see more of the world.

subject: Themberchaud’s true nature
fact: The truth that Themberchaud is being manipulated by the Keepers of the Flame, and that he is not the sovereign he believes himself to be, is a dangerous secret that could collapse the power structure of Gracklstugh if revealed.
source_quote: Themberchaud thinks we work for him. What Themberchaud doesn’t realize is that he works for us.

subject: Themberchaud’s true nature
fact: Whether Themberchaud is a prisoner, a weapon, a deity, or a corrupted guardian is unknown. Grygum’s reverence and Thorin’s willingness to weaponize it suggest it holds deeper significance than mere beasthood — its revelation could shatter Duergar dogma or awaken an ancient power.

subject: The Nature of Psychic Blades
fact: The existence of psychic blades — weapons that kill without physical trace — is confirmed by multiple sources: Daz’s novels, Zalthir’s observations, and the woundless corpses — but their origin, creators, and connection to the Gray Ghosts remain unknown.
source_quote: It leaves no trace.

subject: the proof of the Gray Ghosts
fact: The proof of the Gray Ghosts is a requested item that Gartokkar seeks, but its form or existence is not clarified in this session.
source_quote: Gartokkar looks at him, 'Just find me the egg and the proof of the Gray Ghosts.'

subject: Thorin’s plan to ride the dragon out
fact: Thorin has conceived a radical plan to exploit Themberchaud’s belief in his own autonomy, using him as a weapon to escape Gracklstugh and destroy the factions that control it — a plan that could trigger civil war or mass destruction.
source_quote: So what if we ride this Dragon out of here, laying waste to everything behind us?
